entry.title: iFixit Teardown of MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Reveals Glowing Apple Mechanism
entry.content:
Links: ifixit.com

iFixit has published a teardown of Apple's new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR, offering a detailed look at its tandem OLED display and the four-LED lighting strip responsible for illuminating the newly restored glowing Apple logo. The investigation examines how the laptop achieves a lighter chassis design while introducing a touchscreen and retaining functional Touch ID compatibility during logic board swaps.

Despite improvements such as streamlined lid replacement and reliable hardware swapping, the teardown highlights that components like fans and USB-C ports remain buried beneath the logic board. The device ultimately earned a repairability score of 5 out of 10, constrained by design elements like soldered storage and a keyboard integrated into the top case.

entry.title: US Publishers Lose Ground to Chinese Rivals in Mobile Gaming Market
entry.content:
Links: bloomberg.com

US-based video game publishers are losing market share in the $121 billion global mobile gaming sector to Chinese competitors. Chinese studios have increasingly outpaced American counterparts by producing games more quickly, at a lower cost, and with higher profitability.

Popular titles such as Honor of Kings and Whiteout Survival exemplify the shift, highlighting the advanced operational capabilities and rapid development cycles of Chinese developers. This dynamic has allowed Chinese firms to seize leadership in a lucrative market previously dominated by US companies.

entry.title: SpaceX Announces Starlink Mini 2 with Integrated Swappable Battery
entry.content:
Links: theverge.com | starlink.com | hacker news

SpaceX has announced the Starlink Mini 2, a laptop-sized satellite internet terminal that integrates a dish, Wi-Fi router, and an internal battery into a single device. The terminal supports hot-swapping additional batteries to extend operation beyond its standard 4.5-hour charge and can also be powered via a 60W USB-C connection.

Priced at $999, the unit includes a year of Roam Unlimited service and maintains an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance. Despite the added battery weight, the Mini 2 is thinner than the original Mini, measuring 23.1mm thick compared to the previous version's 38.5mm.

entry.title: Google Fi Introduces Automatic Carrier Switching and Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+
entry.content:
Links: engadget.com

A new "super network" feature from Google Fi enables phones to automatically switch between two different carriers to mitigate connection issues caused by signal dead zones or congestion. The rollout begins with Pixel 9 and newer models using eSIMs, with wider availability expected in 2027. The update also introduces Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+, which switches devices to secure Wi-Fi in areas with poor cellular coverage.

Both features are included at no extra cost for Unlimited Premium and Flexible plan subscribers and will function in over 200 international destinations. Google Fi is also deploying "Ask Fi," an AI-powered support agent within its app to assist with billing and technical troubleshooting. Promotional offers accompanying the launch include rebates for the Pixel 11 Pro for new subscribers.

entry.title: Valve Adds Steam Deck Average FPS Data to Steam Store Pages
entry.content:

Valve has begun displaying average frame rate data and histograms for the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED on various Steam Store pages. This information is compiled from anonymized, opt-in player statistics collected since February and is intended to supplement the "Steam Deck Verified" program by providing more granular performance expectations.

While Valve notes that user settings like VSync or frame rate limits can influence the accuracy of these measurements, the data helps players distinguish between performance levels in "Verified" titles and provides insight into how well "Unsupported" games actually run on the handheld hardware.

entry.title: Omdia Reports Global Tablet Shipments Fell 23 Percent in Q3 2026
entry.content:
Links: omdia.tech.informa.com

Global tablet shipments dropped 23% year over year to 32 million units in the third quarter of 2026, reaching their lowest level in nearly three years, according to research from Omdia. The downturn was led by sharp contractions in the Middle East, China, and Western Europe, driven by persistent supply constraints and waning strategic priority from hardware vendors.

Apple and Samsung retained the top two spots in market share despite significant shipment declines of 28% and 22%, respectively. Lenovo was the sole top-five vendor to achieve growth, increasing shipments by 12% to capture a 12.7% market share, while Xiaomi and Huawei rounded out the top five amid an environment where recent flagship device launches failed to spur broader consumer demand.

entry.title: SAG-AFTRA Introduces Pre-Funding Pitch Interactive Media Agreement
entry.content:
Links: gamedeveloper.com

SAG-AFTRA has launched the Pre-Funding Pitch Interactive Media Agreement, a new framework that allows game developers to hire professional union actors for pre-production pitches and vertical slices. The agreement is designed to help teams secure publisher backing in a competitive market by utilizing professional voice and motion performance talent earlier in development.

Eligibility for the new contract is restricted to projects with no more than 30 percent of their initial production funding secured and explicitly prohibits commercial releases. Industry observers note that the initiative may also help developers avoid relying on generative AI voices during early prototyping phases.
